acceptance_reviewed: The Windows startup task has no execution time limit.
The task still runs as SYSTEM with highest privileges at boot.
Installation failure does not start or explicitly stop a task.
Immediate start failure preserves the registered task for the next boot.

findings.claim: Configuring ExecutionTimeLimit in a second PowerShell step can leave a newly created task with PT72H when configuration fails.
findings.evidence: The original local implementation performed schtasks /Create before required PowerShell configuration. The fix now registers PT0S in the same schtasks /Create /XML operation.

findings.claim: A Task Scheduler Exec action should launch the batch file through cmd.exe.
findings.evidence: The XSD validates Command as a path type but does not prove a .cmd file is directly executable through CreateProcess. The final XML uses cmd.exe with /d /s /c and a quoted script path.

findings.claim: Windows accepts the generated XML, preserves PT0S, runs as SYSTEM, and starts successfully at boot.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions run 31641000991 on windows-latest accepted the UTF-16 task XML, exported PT0S with SYSTEM and highest privileges, confirmed the proxy responding on port 18080, and captured Task Scheduler with cuse. Boot persistence follows from the registered BootTrigger; an actual reboot was not performed.

findings.claim: portless clean can leave Windows service files behind when no task is registered.
findings.evidence: tryUninstallService returns early when schtasks /Query fails, before removing spec.scriptDir. service uninstall does remove the directory and now has direct coverage.

findings.claim: A failed reinstall can update the shared service script before task registration succeeds.
findings.evidence: installService writes portless-service.cmd before schtasks /Create. This ordering predates #378 and requires Windows-specific file replacement and rollback design.

exemptions.claim: README, skills/portless/SKILL.md, and CLI help do not need updates.
exemptions.evidence: The user-facing contract remains a Windows Task Scheduler startup task running as SYSTEM; only its internal registration representation and reliability changed.

issue_candidates.title: Windows clean leaves orphaned service files when task registration failed
issue_candidates.evidence: tryUninstallService returns before fs.rmSync(spec.scriptDir) when schtasks /Query reports no task.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: The behavior predates #378 and is not required to remove the 72-hour execution limit.

issue_candidates.title: Windows reinstall writes service script before task replacement succeeds
issue_candidates.evidence: The shared .cmd is overwritten before schtasks /Create /XML /F reports success.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Safe rollback needs a Windows-specific atomic replacement design and real scheduler validation beyond #378.
